facts.claim: How many times faster than play the mountain's time runs: an hour on the mountain passes in 50 seconds of play. It's six times the scale the route is drawn at (route.drawn-scale), so a climber goes six times as fast as in life over the drawn ground, at a walker's pace on the screen, and still takes a section's real hours on the clock, which their body tires, thirsts and sickens by. Twice the 36 it was first fitted to (an hour in 100 s, the slowest summit day in 20 minutes), which played too slowly (albalaeff, 2026-11-19): now the slowest summit day on record, 12 hours from the South Col to the summit in the queue of 20 May 2026, plays in 10 minutes, and the whole climb in about an hour once camp skips the waits.

facts.question: The sources give each section's hours (time.base-camp-to-camp-1 to time.camp-2-to-base-camp), but they differ by up to two hours, give lengths on the ground only as far as Camp 3, and don't say how much each section climbs. Which hours hold for a client today, the first time and on later rotations; how long is each section on the ground, and how much does it climb? The game draws every section at the same share of life and walks the climber over it at real speed by the mountain's clock, so these hours and lengths are what it has to fit.
